label: Carbon avoided per kg of clothing collected (system-level, lower bound)

provenance.input: What carbon savings per kilogram result from clothing reuse in life cycle assessments?
sourceTitles: Environmental performance of the EPR textile sector (Refashion/Deloitte)

systemBoundary: Full chain: collection, sorting, second-hand reuse and recovery, for clothing and household linen. Second-hand reuse is the main driver.
uncertainty: Lower-bound, system-level average across mixed-quality streams. All textiles including footwear average 2.1; footwear alone only 0.50.

label: Carbon avoided per high or medium-quality garment reused

provenance.input: What carbon savings per kilogram result from clothing reuse in life cycle assessments?
sourceTitles: LCA-based assessment of European used textiles (EuRIC)

systemBoundary: Reuse of a high or medium-quality garment versus new production, including global transport emissions for exported reuse.
uncertainty: Per-garment, not per-kg. Reuse found to be roughly 70 times lower impact than new production for reusable qualities.

label: Carbon avoided per kg of clothing reused (upper bound)

provenance.input: What carbon savings per kilogram result from clothing reuse in life cycle assessments?
sourceTitles: Reusing 1 kg of clothing saves 25 kg of CO2 (UPC INTEXTER)

systemBoundary: Avoided virgin fibre production and manufacturing for the fibres reused.
uncertainty: Upper-bound. Assumes a reused garment fully displaces new production (substitution rate 1), which overstates real-world displacement.

label: Energy avoided per kg of virgin cotton displaced by reuse

provenance.input: What carbon savings per kilogram result from clothing reuse in life cycle assessments?
sourceTitles: LCA of donated textile reuse/recycling, UK energy perspective

unit: kWh saved / kg virgin cotton displaced
systemBoundary: Streamlined energy LCA: extraction, materials, electricity, collection, processing, distribution and disposal, for donated textiles versus virgin material.
uncertainty: Expressed as energy, not CO2e. Converts to carbon by the local grid intensity. Polyester displacement saves roughly 90 kWh per kg.
